source_candidate.identity_note: The sealed worker checkpoint is a prose continuation and does not expose a stable local C-id for the Meta^n subject. This audit is therefore bound to namespace + exact source artifact blob + subject, not a guessed short id.
source_candidate.subject: Meta^n: Recursive Self-Improvement through Emergent Depth

official_repository.release_to_audited_head_delta: one commit, only meta_n/core/omega.py changed (display-precision normalization); all selection, archive, persistence, adapters and consolidation files inspected here are byte-identical to the initial public release.

findings.finding: The public repository is substantial and source-bound closely enough to the paper release for implementation auditing.
evidence: Git history contains an explicit 'Initial public release of Meta^n' commit b0861e6, followed by one commit b708184 that changes only omega.py display normalization.
The repo persists archive candidates, parent_id, iteration, depth, injected code, traces, checkpoint state, config snapshots, summaries and lineage-oriented artifacts.
findings.scope: Supports mechanism/provenance inspection, not the paper's numerical headline reproduction by itself.

findings.finding: The paper's archive-best estimator is genuinely a per-task routed portfolio; it is not the same object as a single deployable lineage.
evidence: archive.py tracks the best trace/source separately for each task and uses those winners in parent selection.
The paper explicitly reports archive-best and best-single-chain separately and describes the gap as the value of letting different tasks be won by different chains.
findings.scope_correction: Do not interpret archive-best as one single improved solver. For benchmarks where task identity is available at deployment, it can correspond to a task-conditioned routed portfolio; otherwise it is an oracle-style upper estimator unless the router is part of the deployment contract.

findings.finding: For adapters with a real test split, held-out test scoring occurs after search and re-executes the selected stored solution on test data; this is materially stronger than using test data inside archive selection.
evidence: EvolutionaryOrchestrator performs a final 'Test Set Evaluation' after search.
_run_test_evaluation chooses per-task dev/archive winners and calls adapter.evaluate_test on their stored scripts.
The paper labels CO-Bench/S2D/LawBench table values as held-out test and plots search curves as validation with test stars after search.
findings.scope_correction: The routed portfolio is selected on development scores, then evaluated on held-out data; this is not direct held-out leakage. It still measures a routed portfolio rather than one lineage.

findings.finding: ARC-AGI-2 has an explicit unresolved proxy-overfit weakness in the released implementation.
evidence: arc_agi.py states evaluate() scores demonstration TRAIN pairs shown to the model, while evaluate_test() scores hidden TEST pairs only at end.
ARCAGI2Adapter.split_type() returns 'proxy' and comments that split-aware overfit protection is not yet consumed: per-task-best still ranks raw dev scores.
EvolutionaryOrchestrator emits a warning that proxy-stable demotion is deferred and raw dev still drives archive selection.
findings.scope_correction: The final ARC test number can remain honest because test outputs are withheld, but candidate selection is especially prone to demonstration overfit. The 0.331 dev/archive-best and held-out result should not be conflated.

findings.finding: The consolidation zero-regression property is primarily a construction invariant, and the public tests strongly support that exact mechanism.
evidence: In consolidate mode each candidate solves one target and deep-copies inherited per-task-best traces for every other task; inherited traces are not re-solved.
tests/test_consolidation.py deliberately injects noisy target regressions and asserts per-task-best/oracle history never decreases.
The forced merged candidate assembles per-task winners and is not a fresh end-to-end re-evaluation.
findings.scope_correction: Zero regression refers to the stored per-task-best trajectory on the selection/evaluation task set under frozen inheritance. It is not an independent held-out no-regression theorem for a newly executed merged system.

findings.finding: The paper's +0.10 consolidation mean-lift result remains primary-study evidence despite strong mechanism tests.
evidence: Paper Appendix G reports 8-task CO-Bench, 3 seeds, 0.502 -> 0.71±0.02, best-of-4 control 0.61±0.03, +0.10 CI [+0.04,+0.16], zero regressions 8/8.
The public repo contains mechanism-level unit/integration tests but no source-matched raw three-seed experiment bundle identified in this audit.
No protocol-matched independent reproduction was found in fresh public search two days after the paper release.
findings.scope: Mechanism A-, numerical experiment exact replay/independent replication C.

findings.finding: The repository preserves candidate chronology well enough for structural replay, but the public release does not by itself provide the paper's full run corpus.
evidence: Candidate summaries persist candidate_id, parent_id, iteration, depth, per-task scores, traces and injected code.
checkpoint.json persists RNG state, token counters, run config snapshot, archive-related control state, and supports resume/rebuild.
README documents candidate directories, logs and summaries as run outputs.
findings.scope_correction: This is good prospective provenance. It does not prove that the exact paper-producing archives/raw LLM I/O for all reported seeds are publicly included.

findings.finding: Exact replay is weakened by environment and dataset immutability gaps.
evidence: pyproject.toml uses broad lower-bound versions for core dependencies such as pydantic>=2.0, openai>=1.0, httpx>=0.25, numpy>=1.24 and pyyaml>=6.0.
data/README states datasets are not bundled; only some upstream sources are commit-pinned, while Hugging Face datasets auto-download without source snapshot hashes documented there.
Paper-scale runs require external models/APIs and benchmark environments not captured as a single immutable public replay bundle.
findings.scope: These gaps do not negate published results; they reduce exact replay readiness.

findings.finding: The file named adoption.py is not the candidate acceptance/selection gate.
evidence: adoption.py implements helper-usage/adoption attribution and failure classification.
Candidate ranking, per-task-best updates, elites and parent selection live in archive.py; gating/search logic lives in evolutionary_orchestrator.py.
findings.scope_correction: Future audits should not infer candidate acceptance policy from adoption.py.

published_claims_checked.recursion_ablation: Paper v1 states CO-Bench archive-best validation falls 0.845 -> 0.714 when recursion is removed; this remains primary-study numerical evidence.
published_claims_checked.archive_vs_chain: Paper v1 reports GPT-5.2 CO-Bench 0.870 archive-best vs 0.806 best chain and ARC-AGI-2 dev 0.331 vs 0.123 (one-seed best chain). Implementation semantics support the estimator distinction.
published_claims_checked.consolidation: Paper v1 reports 8-task/3-seed 0.502 -> 0.71±0.02 and +0.10 vs compute-matched best-of-4 with CI [+0.04,+0.16]. Mechanism is strongly supported; numeric replay remains unverified.
published_claims_checked.heldout: Paper v1 labels CO-Bench/S2D/LawBench table values as held-out tests, while benchmarks without held-out splits report benchmark scores; source implements an end-of-run test pass where adapter support exists.

independent_reproduction_search.result: No protocol-matched independent reproduction of Meta^n headline benchmark or consolidation results was established in fresh web/GitHub search. This is unsurprising given the paper/public release is about two days old.

reproduction_blockers: No identified public raw run bundle binding every headline cell to exact candidate archive, LLM I/O, seed, model endpoint/version, benchmark snapshot and final test outputs.
Core dependency versions are not fully locked.
Several benchmark datasets/environments are downloaded externally and are not all bound to immutable snapshot hashes in the public data guide.
The current public code is source-near to release, but no explicit repository tag/manifest binding paper tables to a specific commit/run bundle was found in this audit.
ARC archive selection currently consumes a leaky proxy dev signal by design.
reopen_conditions: A paper-authored raw run/archive bundle is published with source commit, dataset/container snapshots and exact per-seed outputs.
An independent group publishes protocol-matched reruns of headline or consolidation results.
ARC split-aware proxy overfit protection becomes active and is evaluated without hidden-test selection feedback.
A deployable merged/router artifact is rerun end-to-end on an outer test set rather than inheriting stored per-task traces.
exact_next_action: On the next valid invocation, resolve the then-current sealed ACTIVE_WAVE and audit a different source-qualified non-evaluation candidate. Prefer a candidate with an executable official artifact or raw result bundle that can materially improve independent-reproduction confidence; do not repeat Meta^n unless a reopen condition occurs.
